newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon PM Hariri leaves for Cairo.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon PM Hariri leaves for Cairo.

text.p: Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri left for Cairo on Wednesday night for talks with Egyptian leaders on Middle East peace talks and bilateral trade issues, official sources said.
Official sources said Hariri, who left for the Egyptian capital aboard his private jet, would meet President Hosni Mubarak and other Egyptian officials.

A main issue on the agenda is what Beirut newspapers called a looming crisis between Beirut and Cairo over Lebanon's recent decision to halt imports of potatoes from Egypt, a move that drew sharp criticism from some Egyptian officials.
Lebanon has defended the ban, decided more than two weeks ago, saying it was not aimed at Egypt but to protect home-grown potatoes.

Lebanon's Agriculture Minister Shawki Fakhoury, hours before Hariri's departure, reiterated the ban on the importing of potatoes, saying it included other Arab countries like Syria, Jordan and Saudi Arabia.
"The issue has surpassed the issue of importing potatoes to the grave and mounting imbalance in the agricultural trade balance between Lebanon and Egypt," Fakhoury said.
He said Lebanon has imported from Egypt 31,076 tonnes of agricultural produce in the first three months of 1997 against such exports of only 2,439 tonnes over the same period.

The Lebanese government, trying to cut the cost of its food imports, plans to keep out products that can be grown at home from October 1. Fakhoury has said that the ban on Egyptian potatoes was part of the same plan.
